ARC Lab
AI and Robotics for Construction Laboratory
About Us
Welcome to the AI and Robotics for Construction (ARC) Lab at the Technion – Israel Institute of Technology!
We envision a future in which the built environment is not only digitally represented, but can also be
understood, reasoned about, and acted upon by intelligent systems.
Built environment engineering has largely been shaped around the assumption that its primary agents are human — an assumption embedded in how information is represented, engineering knowledge is formed, processes are structured, and physical production is carried out.
Our research rethinks these foundations:
01
How the built environment should be represented for machine intelligence.
02
How AI systems can learn engineering knowledge from the digital traces of practice.
03
How digital engineering processes are constituted and analyzed.
04
How construction production and management systems must evolve as robots become agents of physical production.

pages.main_text:
Agent-oriented Design and Construction
Overview
We investigate how engineering work in the design and construction of buildings and infrastructure should be reconfigured when AI agents become active participants. Our research aims to develop data representations and digital environments that enable AI agents to understand, reason about, and act within these processes.

pages.main_text:
Interaction-centered Building Information Modeling (IC-BIM)
Overview
We investigate the structure of BIM processes, treating interaction as the basic unit from which complex BIM processes are formed. Our research aims to establish a formal theory that provides a rigorous basis for representing, analyzing, and explaining how BIM processes are organized and evolve, with the potential to generalize to digital engineering processes more broadly.

pages.main_text:
Representation Learning for the Built Environment
Overview
We investigate how engineering knowledge can be learned directly from the BIM models and other digital data generated across the built environment lifecycle. Our research develops representation learning methods that capture patterns, relationships, and latent knowledge in these data, enabling more generalizable and data-driven engineering intelligence.
